Why troy ounces vs standard ounces matter
A "troy ounce" is the standard weight in precious metals —
31.10 grams
.
A standard (avoirdupois) ounce — the one on your kitchen scale — is
28.35 grams
. Treating them as equal gives a ~10% error.
If you buy "an ounce of silver" you're buying a troy ounce. If a coin's
catalog says
"weighs 1 oz"
, in this context it means 1 troy ounce.
Always double-check when the seller is unfamiliar with bullion terminology.
Frequently asked
How many troy ounces are in a kilo?
A kilogram holds 32.1507 troy ounces (1,000 g ÷ 31.1035 g per troy ounce). A standard 1 kg gold or silver bar therefore contains about 32.15 troy oz of metal.
How do you convert troy ounces to pounds?
One troy ounce equals 0.06857 of a standard (avoirdupois) pound, so a standard pound contains 14.583 troy ounces. Note a troy pound is different — it is only 12 troy ounces (373.24 g).
How many grams are in a troy ounce?
One troy ounce is exactly 31.1034768 grams — about 10% heavier than the 28.35 g standard ounce on a kitchen scale.
Is a troy ounce the same as a regular ounce?
No. A troy ounce (31.10 g) is roughly 10% heavier than a standard/avoirdupois ounce (28.35 g). Precious metals are always priced per troy ounce.
